reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent (Claude), combined hunt+verify — confirmed the benchmark exercises all four legs, checked the baseline numbers against the measured host figures, and found+reproduced the int64 overflow dropping ~47% of the 200k dataset
accepted on inspection — the overflow was reproduced by the reviewer (firstBad i=106752, 93248/200000 dropped) and the fix (stride-before-multiply) is verified by re-measuring all 200k in-window

records.finding: int64(i)*int64(span) overflowed (span=24h ~8.6e13 ns): past ~107k events the product wrapped negative, placing events before the window where memq drops them. The events=200000 run measured only ~107k, mislabeling the baseline and faking sub-linear growth.
records.evidence: At: benchWindow.From.Add(time.Duration(int64(i) * int64(span) / int64(nEvents))); reproduced: 93248/200000 events out-of-window
records.reason: Compute the per-event stride (span/nEvents) BEFORE multiplying by i, so no overflow (200k*432M ns = 8.6e13, in range). Re-measured the true baseline (~730 ms/op, ~646 MB/op, ~10M allocs at 200k) and corrected the documented numbers + growth description (roughly linear). 50k was unaffected.
